text.p: Sundstrand Corp, which makes components and subsystems for the aerospace and industrial markets, said Friday it had raised its 1997 earnings forecast by $0.10, to a range of $2.75-$2.95 a share.
The forecast excludes the impact of restructuring charges and any future share repurchases.
In April Sundstrand said it expected earnings for 1997 in a range of $2.65-$2.85 a share.
Sundstrand said it expected 1997 sales to grow by about 15 percent freom 1996, which compares with forecast growth of 10-15 percent in April.
In 1996 the company had operating earnings of $2.30 a share on sales of $1.52 billion.
Sundstrand reported second quarter operating earnings of $0.72 a share, up from $0.53 a year ago. For the first six months, operating earnings rose to $1.30 from $1.00.
Sales for the second quarter increased to $440.0 million from $371.0 million, and for the six months increased to $829.0 million from $739.0 million.
Second quarter aerospace sales were $243 million, up 33 percent from a year ago. Operating profit rose 52 percent to $44 million. Aerospace orders were $388 million, up 63 percent.

"We now expect overall aerospace sales growth to be about 25 percent in 1996, with commercial OEM (original equipment manufacturer) growth of approximately 45 percent," Robert Jenkins, chairman, said in a statement. "Commercial aftermarket should grow by about 15 percent, and military sales are projected to increase by approximately 20 percent."
He said early indications point to growth in aerospace revenues in 1998, but at lower rates than in 1997.
Second quarter industrial sales were $197 million, up five percent from a year ago. Operating profit was $34 million, up 10 percent. Orders fell two percent to $186 million.

"With the lower orders experienced during the second quarter and the continued strength of the U.S. dollar, we now expect industrial revenue growth to be up only slightly for 1997, with operating profit margins in the 16 percent range," Jenkins said.
